dedup.scope: Targeted neighbours only: every public item whose record mentions this DOI, the open/closed Sullivan spaces, arc graphs, PROPs and operads of arc families, string topology or Hochschild complexes, plus the retired-claims list and the preparation worklist, and the same-source counted unit. No global novelty claim.
compared: public 2757 (same source, counted unit): Theorem 5.1 with label discretethm, statement source lines 1249-1254, proofs at 1261-1263 and 1267-1412. It states that the discrete arc-graph correlators define an action respecting every window gluing for basic ordinary Frobenius systems satisfying conditions C and E. That is a statement about correlators and gluings; it says nothing about a CW structure, about cells indexed by arc graphs, about attaching maps, or about a deformation retraction, and none of its counted spans overlaps this task's spans (1575-1580, 1582-1611, 1568-1573).

public 198157 'The topology of Lagrangian submanifolds via open-closed string topology' (arxiv:2604.08481v1, label Lm:dgLieMorphismApp): a lemma producing a dg Lie algebra morphism from an open-closed construction. Different objects and different conclusion; no cell model and no Sullivan space.

public 171354 'Open-closed Deligne--Mumford field theories: geometric foundations' (arxiv:2501.04687v2, label lem:local-exactness-of-delta): a local exactness lemma for the open-closed DM setting, unrelated to arc families or to cell decompositions of section spaces.

public 185747 'Open-closed maps and spectral local systems' (arxiv:2509.21483v2, label prop:truncation-modification): a truncation statement for E-oriented flow categories; the open/closed word is used in a different technical sense.

public 2316 'Automatic split-generation and the quantum-cohomology factor from a smooth Lagrangian endomorphism algebra' (doi:10.5802/jep.290): uses the open-closed isometry and the Hochschild module action to prove split-generation; no arc graphs, no PROPs, no CW model.

public 1432 (doi:10.3842/SIGMA.2021.086, label theo11) and public 2039 (doi:10.5802/jep.142, theorem 1): operadic constructions on typed trees and on Loday realizations of associahedra. Both are operad statements, but their objects are tree operads and polytopal realizations, not weighted arc families on windowed surfaces.
